courses.title: Color
courses.description: Learn to paint with code — fill, stroke, and background colors.

exercises.title: Fill It Up
exercises.description: Color a circle using fill() with RGB values.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a circle filled with hot pink.
Use fill(r, g, b) before circle() to set the color.
Try fill(255, 105, 180) for hot pink.

tasks.title: Add Fill Color
tasks.instruction: Add fill(255, 105, 180) before the circle() call to make it hot pink.

exercises.title: Stroke Story
exercises.description: Add outlines to shapes with stroke() and strokeWeight().
exercises.instruction:
Add a thick red outline to the rectangle.
Use stroke(255, 0, 0) and strokeWeight(5) before rect().

tasks.title: Add Stroke
tasks.instruction: Replace noStroke() with stroke(255, 0, 0) and add strokeWeight(5).

exercises.title: No Fill No Problem
exercises.description: Draw outlines only with noFill(), or filled shapes with noStroke().
exercises.instruction:
Draw two circles side by side.
The left one should be outline-only (noFill + stroke).
The right one should be filled but no outline (fill + noStroke).

tasks.title: Outline Circle
tasks.instruction:
Draw an outline-only circle at (130, 200) with diameter 120.
Use noFill(), stroke(0), strokeWeight(3), then circle(130, 200, 120).

tasks.title: Filled Circle
tasks.instruction:
Draw a filled circle at (270, 200) with no outline.
Use fill(50, 150, 255), noStroke(), then circle(270, 200, 120).

exercises.title: Color Mode Explorer
exercises.description: Switch to HSB color mode for intuitive color selection.
exercises.instruction:
Switch to HSB color mode using colorMode(HSB).
Then fill the circle with a hue-based color: fill(180, 255, 255) for cyan.

tasks.title: Switch to HSB
tasks.instruction: Add colorMode(HSB) in draw(), then use fill(180, 255, 255) to draw a cyan circle.

exercises.title: Background Bliss
exercises.description: Set a custom background color to change the canvas appearance.
exercises.instruction:
Set a dark blue background using background(20, 30, 80).
Then draw a bright yellow circle on top.

tasks.title: Set Background
tasks.instruction: Add background(20, 30, 80) at the start of draw() for a dark blue canvas.

courses.title: Curves
courses.description: Master Bézier and spline curves to create flowing, organic shapes.

exercises.title: Bezier Basics
exercises.description: Draw a Bézier curve connecting two points with control points.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a Bézier curve from (50, 350) to (350, 50).
Use bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4).
Control points: (150, 50) and (250, 350) for a nice S-curve.

tasks.title: Draw the Bezier
tasks.instruction:
Draw a Bézier curve with bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4).
Use (50, 350), (150, 50), (250, 350), (350, 50).

exercises.title: Spline Stroke
exercises.description: Draw a spline curve through a series of points (p5.js v2).
exercises.instruction:
Draw a smooth spline curve passing through four points.
Use spline(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4) — the v2 name for what was curve().
Points: (40, 300), (140, 80), (260, 320), (360, 100).

tasks.title: Draw the Spline
tasks.instruction:
Draw a spline with spline(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4).
Use (40, 300), (140, 80), (260, 320), (360, 100).
Note: spline() is the p5.js v2 name for the old curve() function.

exercises.title: Curve Points
exercises.description: Use bezierPoint() to calculate and plot individual points along a Bézier curve.
exercises.instruction:
Plot 10 evenly-spaced dots along a Bézier curve.
Use bezierPoint(x1, x2, x3, x4, t) to get the x and y coordinates at parameter t (0 to 1).
Draw a small circle at each computed point.

tasks.title: Compute Points
tasks.instruction:
Inside the loop, use bezierPoint() to compute the x and y coordinates.
Let px = bezierPoint(x1, x2, x3, x4, t) and py = bezierPoint(y1, y2, y3, y4, t).

tasks.title: Draw the Dots
tasks.instruction:
Draw a circle at each computed point using circle(px, py, 12).
You should see 11 dots (including t=0 and t=1) tracing the Bézier curve.

exercises.title: Tangent Lines
exercises.description: Use bezierTangent() to draw tangent lines along a Bézier curve.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a Bézier curve and add tangent lines at several points.
Use bezierTangent(x1, x2, x3, x4, t) to get the tangent direction.
Normalize the tangent and draw short lines extending from each point on the curve.

tasks.title: Compute Tangents
tasks.instruction:
Use bezierTangent(x1, x2, x3, x4, t) to get the tangent x and y components.
Store them as tx and ty.

tasks.title: Draw Tangent Lines
tasks.instruction:
Draw a line from each point on the curve in the tangent direction.
Use line(px, py, px + tx * 20, py + ty * 20) to extend 20 pixels along the tangent.

courses.title: Custom Shapes
courses.description: Build custom shapes with vertex-based drawing using beginShape() and endShape().

exercises.title: Vertex Playground
exercises.description: Use beginShape(), vertex(), and endShape() to draw a custom polygon.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a triangle using vertex coordinates.
Use beginShape(), three vertex(x, y) calls, and endShape(CLOSE).
Vertices: (200, 60), (80, 340), (320, 340).

tasks.title: Add Vertex Calls
tasks.instruction:
Add three vertex(x, y) calls between beginShape() and endShape(CLOSE).
Use (200, 60), (80, 340), and (320, 340).

exercises.title: Polygon Party
exercises.description: Draw a pentagon by placing five vertices around a center point.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a regular pentagon centered at (200, 220) with a radius of about 140.
Use beginShape(), five vertex() calls, and endShape(CLOSE).
Vertices: (200, 80), (333, 171), (283, 336), (117, 336), (67, 171).

tasks.title: Draw the Pentagon
tasks.instruction:
Add five vertex(x, y) calls between beginShape() and endShape(CLOSE).
Use the coordinates: (200, 80), (333, 171), (283, 336), (117, 336), (67, 171).

exercises.title: Bezier Blob
exercises.description: Create curved shapes using bezierVertex() inside beginShape().
exercises.instruction:
Draw a curved blob using bezierVertex() for smooth sides.
Use beginShape(), then alternate vertex() and bezierVertex() calls.
Start at (100, 200), use bezierVertex() for the top and bottom curves, and close the shape.

tasks.title: First Bezier Curve
tasks.instruction:
Add three bezierVertex() calls to create the top curve of the blob.
In p5.js v2 each bezierVertex(x, y) call sets one control point.
Use bezierVertex(100, 50), bezierVertex(300, 50), and bezierVertex(300, 200).

tasks.title: Complete the Blob
tasks.instruction:
Add three more bezierVertex() calls to create the bottom curve.
Use bezierVertex(300, 350), bezierVertex(100, 350), and
bezierVertex(100, 200) to loop back to the start.

exercises.title: Spline Smoothie
exercises.description: Use splineVertex() for automatically smooth curves through your points.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a smooth wavy shape using splineVertex() (p5.js v2).
Use beginShape(), add at least 4 splineVertex() calls, and endShape(CLOSE).
splineVertex() creates smooth Catmull-Rom splines through your points.

tasks.title: Add Spline Vertices
tasks.instruction:
Add at least 4 splineVertex(x, y) calls between beginShape() and endShape(CLOSE).
Try placing points around a circle-like path for a smooth blob.

courses.title: Data Storage
courses.description: Save and retrieve data with localStorage to persist state across sessions.

exercises.title: Store It
exercises.description: Save a value to localStorage using storeItem().
exercises.instruction:
Use storeItem("myColor", "blue") to save a color string.
Then use getItem("myColor") to retrieve it and display with text().

tasks.title: Store and Retrieve
tasks.instruction:
In setup(), add storeItem("myColor", "blue").
In draw(), use let saved = getItem("myColor") and display it with text().

exercises.title: Click Counter
exercises.description: Count clicks and persist the count across page reloads.
exercises.instruction:
Use a variable count initialized from getItem("count") || 0.
In mousePressed(), increment count and storeItem("count", count).
Display the count on screen.

tasks.title: Persist Click Count
tasks.instruction:
In setup(), load count from getItem("count") || 0.
Create mousePressed() to increment and storeItem("count", count).

exercises.title: Clear It All
exercises.description: Clear all stored data with clearStorage().
exercises.instruction:
Store a value with storeItem(), display it, then call clearStorage() in mousePressed().
After clearing, getItem() should return null.

tasks.title: Clear Storage on Click
tasks.instruction: Create mousePressed() that calls clearStorage() to remove all stored items.

courses.title: DOM Elements
courses.description: Create interactive UI elements outside the canvas with sliders, buttons, checkboxes, and color pickers.

exercises.title: Slider Sense
exercises.description: Use createSlider() to control the size of a circle in real time.
exercises.instruction:
Create a slider that controls the diameter of a circle.
Use createSlider(min, max, value) with range 10 to 200, default 80.
Read its value with slider.value() in draw().

tasks.title: Create a Slider
tasks.instruction:
Call createSlider(10, 200, 80) in setup() and store it in a variable.
This creates a slider with min=10, max=200, and default value=80.

tasks.title: Read Slider Value
tasks.instruction:
In draw(), call slider.value() to get the current slider position.
Use that value as the diameter in circle(200, 200, d).

exercises.title: Button Bonanza
exercises.description: Use createButton() to make a clickable button that triggers an action.
exercises.instruction:
Create a button that changes the canvas background when clicked.
Use createButton(label) and .mousePressed() to toggle a background color.

tasks.title: Create a Button
tasks.instruction: Call createButton("Toggle") in setup() and store it in a variable.

tasks.title: Attach Event
tasks.instruction: Call btn.mousePressed() with a callback function that toggles bgColor between 30 and 220.

exercises.title: Checkbox Charm
exercises.description: Use createCheckbox() to toggle the fill of a shape on and off.
exercises.instruction:
Create a checkbox that toggles between a filled circle and an outlined circle.
Use createCheckbox(label) and .checked() to read its state.

tasks.title: Create Checkbox
tasks.instruction: Call createCheckbox("Fill", true) in setup() to create a checked checkbox.

tasks.title: Toggle Fill
tasks.instruction:
In draw(), use an if statement with cb.checked() to call fill() or noFill().
Then draw a circle at (200, 200) with diameter 150.

exercises.title: Color Picker Party
exercises.description: Use createColorPicker() to let the user choose a fill color interactively.
exercises.instruction:
Create a color picker that controls the fill of a shape.
Use createColorPicker(defaultColor) and .color() to read the chosen color.

tasks.title: Create Color Picker
tasks.instruction:
Call createColorPicker("#ff64c8") in setup() and store it in a variable.
This creates a color picker with a pink default color.

tasks.title: Apply Picked Color
tasks.instruction:
In draw(), call fill(picker.color()) to use the picked color.
Draw a rounded rect(100, 100, 200, 200, 20) with that fill.

courses.title: Events
courses.description: Make your sketches respond to mouse clicks, key presses, and touch.

exercises.title: Click to Draw
exercises.description: Draw a circle where the user clicks using mousePressed().
exercises.instruction:
Define a mousePressed() function that draws a circle at mouseX, mouseY.
Each time you tap the canvas, a new circle appears.

tasks.title: Define mousePressed
tasks.instruction:
Create a mousePressed() function that draws a circle at mouseX, mouseY.
Use fill(255, 100, 150), noStroke(), circle(mouseX, mouseY, 40).

exercises.title: Key Mapper
exercises.description: Change canvas color based on which key is pressed.
exercises.instruction:
Define a keyPressed() function.
If key === "r", set background to red.
If key === "g", set background to green.
If key === "b", set background to blue.

tasks.title: Define keyPressed
tasks.instruction: Create a keyPressed() function that changes background color based on the key variable.

exercises.title: Draggable Dot
exercises.description: Draw a circle that follows the mouse when pressed.
exercises.instruction:
In draw(), check if mouseIsPressed is true.
If so, draw a circle at mouseX, mouseY.
This creates a drawing-while-dragging effect.

tasks.title: Mouse Pressed Check
tasks.instruction: In draw(), add: if (mouseIsPressed) { fill(255, 50, 100); noStroke(); circle(mouseX, mouseY, 30); }

exercises.title: Arrow Mover
exercises.description: Move a shape with arrow keys using keyIsDown().
exercises.instruction:
Create a variable x = 200, y = 200.
In draw(), check keyIsDown(LEFT_ARROW), keyIsDown(RIGHT_ARROW), etc. to move x and y.
Draw a circle at x, y.

tasks.title: Arrow Key Movement
tasks.instruction:
In draw(), add keyIsDown checks for all four arrows to update x and y.
Use LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW, UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW constants.

courses.title: Image
courses.description: Create, display, and manipulate images on the canvas.

exercises.title: Pixel Canvas
exercises.description: Create an image from scratch by setting individual pixels.
exercises.instruction:
Create a 100x100 image and fill the top half with red.
Use createImage(w, h) to make the image,
set(x, y, color) to set a red pixel, then updatePixels().

tasks.title: Create an Image
tasks.instruction: Create a 100x100 image using createImage(100, 100).

tasks.title: Set Pixels
tasks.instruction:
Call loadPixels() on the image, then use a loop to set pixels in the top half (y < 50) to red using set(x, y, color(255, 0, 0)).
Finish with updatePixels().

exercises.title: Image Tint
exercises.description: Display an image with a color tint.
exercises.instruction:
Create a colored image and display it with a tint.
Use createImage(w, h), fill it with a color, then use
tint(r, g, b) before image(img, x, y).

tasks.title: Display Image
tasks.instruction: Create a 100x100 image, fill all pixels white (255, 255, 255), and display it with image(img, 150, 150).

tasks.title: Apply Tint
tasks.instruction: Use tint(255, 200, 0) before the image() call to tint the image yellow.

exercises.title: Filter Fun
exercises.description: Apply built-in filters to the canvas.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a shape and apply a filter to the entire canvas.
Use filter(GRAY) after drawing to turn the canvas grayscale.

tasks.title: Apply Gray Filter
tasks.instruction: After drawing the red circle, add filter(GRAY) to convert the canvas to grayscale.

tasks.title: Try Invert
tasks.instruction: Change filter(GRAY) to filter(INVERT) to invert the canvas colors.

exercises.title: Pixel Peek
exercises.description: Read pixel colors from the canvas.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a shape and use get(x, y) to read a pixel color.
get(x, y) returns a p5.Color object at the given coordinates.

tasks.title: Get a Pixel
tasks.instruction: Use get(200, 200) to read the center pixel color into a variable named c.

tasks.title: Use the Pixel
tasks.instruction:
Use fill(c) to set the fill color to the sampled pixel,
then draw a 50x50 rectangle at (300, 300) to display the sampled color.

courses.title: Loading Data
courses.description: Load and display external data like JSON and images in your sketches.

exercises.title: JSON Display
exercises.description: Load a JSON resource and display its values on canvas.
exercises.instruction:
Use loadJSON() with an async setup() to load embedded data.
In draw(), use text() to display data values on canvas.

tasks.title: Load and Display JSON
tasks.instruction:
Make setup() async and use await loadJSON() with the data: URL to load data.
In draw(), check if data exists and display it with text().

exercises.title: Image Loader
exercises.description: Load an image and display it on canvas.
exercises.instruction:
Use loadImage() with an async setup() to load an embedded image.
In draw(), use image() to draw it on canvas.

tasks.title: Load and Draw Image
tasks.instruction:
Declare a variable img. Make setup() async and use await loadImage() with the data: URL.
In draw(), display it with image(img, 100, 100, 200, 200).

exercises.title: String Loader
exercises.description: Load text data and display it on canvas.
exercises.instruction:
Use loadStrings() with an async setup() to load embedded text.
In draw(), join the array and display with text().

tasks.title: Display Loaded Text
tasks.instruction:
Make setup() async and use await loadStrings() with the data: URL to store lines.
In draw(), display with text(lines.join("\n"), 50, 50, 300, 300).

courses.title: Math
courses.description: Harness p5.js math functions to create dynamic, interactive visuals driven by numbers.

exercises.title: Map Master
exercises.description: Map values from one range to another with map().
exercises.instruction:
Use map() to translate mouseX (0–400) into a circle diameter (20–200).
Draw the circle at the center of the canvas.

tasks.title: Use map() for Diameter
tasks.instruction:
Use map() to map mouseX from the range 0–400 to a diameter range of 20–200.
Store the result in a variable called `d`.

tasks.title: Visual Output
tasks.instruction:
Move your finger across the screen. The circle should grow and shrink
based on the horizontal position.

exercises.title: Constrain King
exercises.description: Keep values within bounds using constrain().
exercises.instruction:
Draw a circle that follows mouseX but never leaves the canvas.
Use constrain() to clamp the x position between 50 and 350.

tasks.title: Use constrain()
tasks.instruction:
Use constrain() to clamp mouseX between 50 and 350.
Store the result in a variable called `x`.

tasks.title: Bounded Circle
tasks.instruction:
The circle should follow your finger horizontally but stop
50 pixels from each edge of the canvas.

exercises.title: Lerp Lab
exercises.description: Smoothly interpolate between values with lerp().
exercises.instruction:
Use lerp() to smoothly move a circle from x=50 toward mouseX each frame.
The circle will trail behind the cursor with easing.

tasks.title: Lerp the Position
tasks.instruction:
Use lerp() to smoothly interpolate `x` toward mouseX each frame.
Use an amount of 0.08 for gentle easing.
Reassign the result back to `x`.

tasks.title: Smooth Motion
tasks.instruction:
The circle should glide smoothly toward your finger position,
never jumping directly to it.

exercises.title: Distance Demo
exercises.description: Measure the distance between two points with dist().
exercises.instruction:
Draw a fixed circle at (200, 200) and a moving circle that follows mouseX.
Use dist() to measure the distance between them and change color based on proximity.

tasks.title: Use dist()
tasks.instruction:
Use dist() to calculate the distance between mouseX, 200 and the fixed point 200, 200.
Store the result in a variable called `d`.

tasks.title: Color by Distance
tasks.instruction:
Use map() to map the distance `d` from 0–200 to a red value from 255–0.
Apply it as the red channel in fill() for the moving circle.

exercises.title: Angle Dance
exercises.description: Use sin() and cos() to create circular motion.
exercises.instruction:
Use sin() and cos() with frameCount to move a circle in a circular orbit.
The circle should orbit around the center of the canvas.

tasks.title: Circular Orbit
tasks.instruction:
Create an `angle` variable using frameCount * 0.05.
Use cos(angle) and sin(angle) to compute x and y positions
that orbit around (200, 200) with a radius of 100.

tasks.title: Orbiting Circle
tasks.instruction:
The circle should continuously orbit around the center of the canvas
in a smooth circular path as frames advance.

courses.title: Random & Noise
courses.description: Explore randomness and noise functions to create organic, unpredictable visuals.

exercises.title: Lucky Draw
exercises.description: Use random() to place a circle at a random position on the canvas.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a circle at a random position using random(low, high).
Set a randomSeed() in setup() so the result is reproducible.
Use randomSeed(42) then random(50, 350) for both x and y.

tasks.title: Seeded Random Position
tasks.instruction:
Use randomSeed(42) in setup() so the result is reproducible.
Use random(50, 350) to generate x and y values, then draw a circle
at those coordinates with diameter 80.

exercises.title: Gaussian Guy
exercises.description: Use randomGaussian() to create a bell-curve distribution of shapes.
exercises.instruction:
Draw 200 small circles whose x-positions follow a Gaussian distribution.
Use randomGaussian(mean, sd) with mean=200 and sd=50.
Use randomSeed(7) for reproducibility.

tasks.title: Gaussian X Position
tasks.instruction:
Inside setup(), draw 200 circles in a for loop.
For each circle, set x = randomGaussian(200, 50) and y = random(50, 350).
Use circle(x, y, 10) for each dot.

exercises.title: Noise Terrain
exercises.description: Use noise() and noiseDetail() to generate an organic terrain grid.
exercises.instruction:
Create a grid of rectangles colored by Perlin noise.
Use noise(x * 0.1, y * 0.1) to get a value between 0 and 1,
then multiply by 255 for brightness. Use noiseDetail(4, 0.5) for texture.

tasks.title: Noise Grid
tasks.instruction:
Create a nested for loop that steps through the canvas in increments of 20.
For each cell, call noise(x * 0.1, y * 0.1) and map it to a fill color.
Draw a rect(x, y, 20, 20) for each cell.

tasks.title: Noise Detail
tasks.instruction:
Add noiseDetail(4, 0.5) in setup() to control the noise quality.
The first parameter is octaves, the second is falloff.

exercises.title: Noise Flow
exercises.description: Animate a circle's position over time using noise and frameCount.
exercises.instruction:
Move a circle across the canvas using noise() driven by frameCount.
Use noise(frameCount * 0.01) * width for x and noise(frameCount * 0.01 + 100) * height for y.

tasks.title: Noise-Driven Position
tasks.instruction:
Generate x and y using noise() with frameCount as input.
Multiply noise output by width/height to map to canvas coordinates.
Draw a circle at those positions with diameter 40.

tasks.title: Offset the Noise
tasks.instruction:
Add an offset of 100 to the y noise input so x and y move independently.
Use noise(frameCount * 0.01 + 100) for the y coordinate.

courses.title: Shapes
courses.description: Master the coordinate system and draw your first primitive shapes using code.

exercises.title: The First Circle
exercises.description: Draw your first shape — a pink ball on a white canvas.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a circle at the center of the 400x400 canvas.
Use circle(x, y, diameter) with x=200, y=200, and a diameter of 100.

tasks.title: Draw the Circle
tasks.instruction:
Draw a circle at the center of the 400x400 canvas.
Use circle(x, y, diameter) with x=200, y=200, and a diameter of 100.

tasks.title: Change the Color
tasks.instruction:
Now change the fill color to orange.
Use fill(255, 165, 0) before the circle() call.

exercises.title: Rectangle Rebel
exercises.description: Learn how to draw rectangles and understand the coordinate system.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a rectangle in the center of the dark canvas.
Use rect(x, y, width, height) to draw a 200x200 rectangle at position (100, 100).

tasks.title: Basic Rectangle
tasks.instruction:
Draw a rectangle at (100, 100) that is 200 wide and 200 tall.
Use rect(x, y, width, height).

tasks.title: Rounded Corners
tasks.instruction:
Add a corner radius of 20 to round the corners.
Use rect(x, y, w, h, radius) with 5 arguments.

exercises.title: Elliptical Motion
exercises.description: Explore the difference between circles and ellipses.
exercises.instruction:
Draw an oval shape that is wider than it is tall.
Use ellipse(x, y, width, height) — try 300 wide and 150 tall, centered at (200, 200).

tasks.title: Basic Ellipse
tasks.instruction:
Draw an ellipse at (200, 200) that is 300 wide and 150 tall.
Use ellipse(x, y, width, height).

tasks.title: Circle via Ellipse
tasks.instruction:
When width equals height, an ellipse becomes a circle.
Draw a perfect circle using ellipse() — set both width and height to 300.

exercises.title: Line Dance
exercises.description: Connect points across the canvas using lines and customize them.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a diagonal line from top-left to bottom-right.
Use line(x1, y1, x2, y2) with coordinates (0, 0) and (400, 400).

tasks.title: Single Line
tasks.instruction:
Draw a diagonal line from top-left (0, 0) to bottom-right (400, 400).
Use line(x1, y1, x2, y2).

tasks.title: Add a Second Line
tasks.instruction:
Draw another line from bottom-left to top-right: (0, 400) to (400, 0).
You now have two line() calls creating an X shape.

exercises.title: Triangle Trouble
exercises.description: Build custom polygons by placing three vertices.
exercises.instruction:
Draw an upward-pointing triangle.
Use triangle(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3) with vertices at (200, 50), (100, 300), and (300, 300).

tasks.title: Basic Triangle
tasks.instruction:
Draw an upward-pointing triangle.
Use triangle(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3) with vertices at (200, 50), (100, 300), (300, 300).

exercises.title: Quad Squad
exercises.description: Draw four-sided shapes with quad() and explore quadrilaterals.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a trapezoid using four corner points.
Use quad(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4) with the given coordinates.

tasks.title: Basic Quad
tasks.instruction:
Draw a trapezoid using four corner points.
Use quad(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4) with vertices at (150, 100), (250, 100), (300, 300), (100, 300).

exercises.title: Arc Adept
exercises.description: Draw partial curves with arc() and control the visible portion.
exercises.instruction:
Draw a semicircle that opens upward.
Use arc(x, y, w, h, start, stop) with PI as the start angle and TWO_PI as the stop angle.

tasks.title: Semicircle
tasks.instruction:
Draw a semicircle that opens upward.
Use arc(x, y, w, h, PI, TWO_PI) with a 300x300 size.

tasks.title: Pie Slice
tasks.instruction:
Add the PIE mode to fill the arc as a pie shape.
Use arc(x, y, w, h, start, stop, PIE) with 7 arguments.

courses.title: Time & Date
courses.description: Use time functions to create animations and display clocks.

exercises.title: Millisecond Counter
exercises.description: Display elapsed time using millis().
exercises.instruction:
Use text() to display the elapsed milliseconds on screen.
Use text("Time: " + millis(), 50, 200) to show a running timer.

tasks.title: Show Millis
tasks.instruction: Add text("Time: " + millis(), 50, 200) to display the running timer.

exercises.title: Pulsing Circle
exercises.description: Create a pulsing circle using sin() with millis().
exercises.instruction:
Use sin(millis() / 500) to create a pulsing effect.
Map the result to a diameter between 50 and 200 using map().

tasks.title: Pulsing Effect
tasks.instruction: Use let pulse = sin(millis() / 500) and let d = map(pulse, -1, 1, 50, 200) to animate circle size.

exercises.title: Frame Counter
exercises.description: Display the frame count and create frame-based animation.
exercises.instruction:
Display frameCount as text on screen.
Also use frameCount to rotate a rectangle: rotate(frameCount * 0.02).

tasks.title: Frame-Based Rotation
tasks.instruction: Show frameCount with text() and use it to rotate a rectangle with push/pop, translate, and rotate.

courses.title: Transform
courses.description: Move, rotate, and scale shapes using transformations.

exercises.title: Slide Into Place
exercises.description: Reposition shapes using translate() instead of hardcoded coordinates.
exercises.instruction:
Use translate(150, 150) to move the origin, then draw a rectangle at (0, 0).
The rectangle will appear at (150, 150) on screen.

tasks.title: Translate and Draw
tasks.instruction: Add translate(150, 150) before rect(0, 0, 100, 100).

exercises.title: Spin Class
exercises.description: Rotate shapes around a point using rotate() with push/pop.
exercises.instruction:
Use push() and pop() to isolate the rotation.
Inside, translate to center, rotate by PI/4 (45 degrees), then draw a rectangle.

tasks.title: Rotate a Rectangle
tasks.instruction: Use push(), translate(200, 200), rotate(PI / 4), rectMode(CENTER), rect(0, 0, 150, 80), pop().

exercises.title: Scale Up
exercises.description: Make shapes bigger or smaller using scale().
exercises.instruction:
Use push/pop with translate to center, then scale(2) to double the size.
Draw a small 50x50 rectangle — it will appear as 100x100.

tasks.title: Scale a Rectangle
tasks.instruction: Use push(), translate(200, 200), scale(2), rectMode(CENTER), rect(0, 0, 50, 50), pop().

exercises.title: State Stack
exercises.description: Use push() and pop() to isolate transforms between multiple shapes.
exercises.instruction:
Draw two rectangles with different transforms.
First: translate(100, 200) + rotate(PI/6), wrapped in push/pop.
Second: translate(300, 200) + scale(1.5), wrapped in push/pop.

tasks.title: Two Transformed Shapes
tasks.instruction:
Draw two rectangles with different transforms using push/pop to isolate them.
First: push, translate(100, 200), rotate(PI/6), fill(255, 100, 100), rect(0,0,80,80), pop.
Second: push, translate(300, 200), scale(1.5), fill(100, 100, 255), rect(0,0,80,80), pop.

courses.title: Typography
courses.description: Learn to draw and style text on the canvas using p5.js typography functions.

exercises.title: Hello World
exercises.description: Display text on the canvas for the first time.
exercises.instruction:
Draw the word "Hello" at the center of the 400x400 canvas.
Use text(str, x, y) with x=200, y=200.

tasks.title: Draw Text
tasks.instruction:
Draw the word "Hello" at coordinates (200, 200).
Use text(str, x, y).

exercises.title: Size Matters
exercises.description: Control the size of your text.
exercises.instruction:
Make the text larger by setting the text size.
Use textSize(size) before your text() call.

tasks.title: Set Text Size
tasks.instruction: Set the text size to 64 using textSize(64) before the text() call.

exercises.title: Style Points
exercises.description: Apply bold and italic styles to your text.
exercises.instruction:
Make the text bold using textStyle().
Use textStyle(BOLD) before the text() call.

tasks.title: Bold Text
tasks.instruction: Set the text style to BOLD using textStyle(BOLD) before text().

exercises.title: Align Right
exercises.description: Control how text is aligned relative to its position.
exercises.instruction:
Right-align text on the canvas.
Use textAlign(RIGHT) before the text() call.

tasks.title: Right Align
tasks.instruction: Set text alignment to RIGHT using textAlign(RIGHT) before text().

exercises.title: Leading Lines
exercises.description: Control the spacing between lines of multi-line text.
exercises.instruction:
Draw multi-line text with custom line spacing.
Use textLeading(n) to set the distance between lines,
then pass a string with \n to text().

tasks.title: Set Line Spacing
tasks.instruction: Set the line spacing to 40 using textLeading(40) before the text() call.

courses.title: Vectors
courses.description: Use p5.Vector to store positions, directions, and perform math on movement.

exercises.title: Vector Basics
exercises.description: Create and use vectors to position shapes on the canvas.
exercises.instruction:
Use createVector() to store the position of a circle.
Access .x and .y to draw it at (200, 300).

tasks.title: Create a Vector
tasks.instruction:
Use createVector() to create a vector with x=200 and y=300.
Store it in a variable called `pos`.

tasks.title: Access Properties
tasks.instruction:
Use pos.x and pos.y as the first two arguments to circle().
The circle should appear at (200, 300).

exercises.title: Vector Math
exercises.description: Combine vectors with add, sub, and mult to move shapes.
exercises.instruction:
Create two vectors and use v.add(), v.sub(), and v.mult()
to compute a final position. Draw the result.

tasks.title: Use Vector Math
tasks.instruction:
Create vector `a` at (300, 200) and vector `b` at (100, 100).
Call a.sub(b) to subtract b from a, then a.mult(1.5).

tasks.title: Draw the Result
tasks.instruction:
Draw a circle at the resulting vector position using a.x and a.y.
After subtracting (100, 100) from (300, 200) and multiplying by 1.5,
the circle should be at (300, 150).

exercises.title: Magnitude Check
exercises.description: Control movement speed with mag(), normalize(), and setMag().
exercises.instruction:
Create a velocity vector and use normalize() and setMag()
to control its speed. Move a circle across the canvas.

tasks.title: Normalize and SetMag
tasks.instruction:
Call vel.normalize() to reduce the velocity to unit length,
then vel.setMag(3) to set a consistent speed of 3 pixels per frame.

tasks.title: Move and Draw
tasks.instruction:
Call pos.add(vel) each frame to update position, then draw the circle.
Wrap back to the left edge when pos.x exceeds 400.

exercises.title: Heading Home
exercises.description: Orient shapes with heading() and rotate() using vector angles.
exercises.instruction: Use heading() to find the angle toward the mouse and rotate() a shape to face it.

tasks.title: Calculate Heading
tasks.instruction:
Create a direction vector from the canvas center (200, 200) to the mouse.
Call heading() on it to get the angle. Store it in `angle`.

tasks.title: Rotate and Draw
tasks.instruction:
Use translate(200, 200) and rotate(angle) before drawing.
Draw a triangle pointing upward that rotates to face the mouse.

courses.title: WebGL Basics
courses.description: Enter the third dimension — draw 3D shapes and control the camera.

exercises.title: Hello 3D
exercises.description: Create a WebGL canvas and draw a rotating box.
exercises.instruction:
Change createCanvas(400, 400, WEBGL) to use WebGL mode.
Use rotateX(frameCount * 0.01) and rotateY(frameCount * 0.01) to spin a box.

tasks.title: Spinning Box
tasks.instruction: Add rotateX(frameCount * 0.01), rotateY(frameCount * 0.01), and box(100) in draw().

exercises.title: Orbit Control
exercises.description: Let the user orbit around a 3D shape with mouse/touch.
exercises.instruction:
Add orbitControl() in draw() to let the user drag to rotate the view.
Draw a sphere() with normalMaterial() for colorful shading.

tasks.title: Interactive 3D
tasks.instruction: Add orbitControl(), normalMaterial(), and sphere(100) in draw().

exercises.title: 3D Primitives
exercises.description: Draw multiple 3D primitives in a scene with lighting.
exercises.instruction:
Add lights() for default lighting.
Draw a cone(), cylinder(), and torus() side by side using translate().
Use push/pop to isolate each shape's position.

tasks.title: Three 3D Shapes
tasks.instruction:
Use push/pop with translate to draw cone(-120,0,0), cylinder(0,0,0), and torus(120,0,0).
Add lights() and orbitControl() for interactivity.

arc.name: arc
arc.description: Draws an arc on the canvas.
arc.syntax: arc(x, y, w, h, start, stop, [mode], [detail])

circle.name: circle

ellipse.name: ellipse
ellipse.description: Draws an ellipse (oval) on the canvas.

line.name: line

point.name: point
point.description: Draws a single point in space.

quad.name: quad

rect.name: rect
rect.description: Draws a rectangle on the canvas.

params.name: h

square.name: square

triangle.name: triangle
triangle.description: Draws a triangle defined by three vertices.

ellipseMode.name: ellipseMode

rectMode.name: rectMode
rectMode.description: Changes where rectangles and squares are drawn.

strokeWeight.name: strokeWeight
strokeWeight.description: Sets the width of the stroke used for points, lines, and the outlines of shapes.

stroke.name: stroke
stroke.description: Sets the color used to draw points, lines, and the outlines of shapes.

params.name: v1
params.description: gray value, red value, or hue.

fill.name: fill
fill.description: Sets the color used to fill shapes.

params.name: v1
params.description: gray value, red value, or hue.

background.name: background
background.description: Sets the color used for the background of the canvas.

params.name: v1
params.description: gray value, red value, or hue.

noStroke.name: noStroke
noStroke.description: Disables drawing points, lines, and the outlines of shapes.

noFill.name: noFill
noFill.description: Disables setting the fill color for shapes.

params.name: v1
params.description: gray value, red value, or hue.

colorMode.name: colorMode
colorMode.description: Changes the way color values are interpreted.

createCanvas.name: createCanvas
createCanvas.description: Creates a canvas element on the web page.

params.name: width
params.description: width of the canvas. Defaults to 100.

params.name: height
params.description: height of the canvas. Defaults to 100.

params.name: renderer
params.description: either P2D or WEBGL. Defaults to P2D.

resizeCanvas.name: resizeCanvas
resizeCanvas.description: Resizes the canvas to a given width and height.

setup.name: setup
setup.description: Called once when the sketch starts, used to define initial properties.

draw.name: draw
draw.description: Called continuously after setup, executes the main drawing code.

preload.name: preload
preload.description: Called before setup, used to load external assets.

loop.name: loop
loop.description: Resumes the draw loop after noLoop has stopped it.

noLoop.name: noLoop
noLoop.description: Stops the draw loop from continuously executing.

redraw.name: redraw
redraw.description: Executes the draw function once when noLoop is active.

push.name: push
push.description: Begins a drawing group that contains its own styles and transformations.

pop.name: pop
pop.description: Ends a drawing group that contains its own styles and transformations.

print.name: print
print.description: Displays text in the web browser's console.

params.name: contents
params.description: the content to print to the console.

frameCount.name: frameCount
frameCount.description: A Number variable that tracks the number of frames drawn since the sketch started.

frameRate.name: frameRate
frameRate.description: Sets the number of frames to draw per second.

mouseX.name: mouseX
mouseX.description: A Number variable that stores the current horizontal position of the mouse.

mouseY.name: mouseY
mouseY.description: A Number variable that stores the current vertical position of the mouse.

mousePressed.name: mousePressed
mousePressed.description: Called when the mouse button is pressed.

mouseReleased.name: mouseReleased
mouseReleased.description: Called when the mouse button is released.

mouseMoved.name: mouseMoved
mouseMoved.description: Called when the mouse is moved.

keyPressed.name: keyPressed
keyPressed.description: Called when a key is pressed.

keyReleased.name: keyReleased
keyReleased.description: Called when a key is released.

keyTyped.name: keyTyped
keyTyped.description: Called when a typed key is detected.

width.name: width
width.description: A Number variable that stores the width of the canvas in pixels.

height.name: height
height.description: A Number variable that stores the height of the canvas in pixels.

random.name: random
random.description: Returns a random number or picks a random item from an array.

params.name: low
params.description: lower bound or array to pick from.

randomSeed.name: randomSeed
randomSeed.description: Sets the seed value for random().

params.name: seed
params.description: seed value for the random number generator.

floor.name: floor
floor.description: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to the value.

ceil.name: ceil
ceil.description: Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the value.

round.name: round
round.description: Returns the value rounded to the nearest integer.

map.name: map
map.description: Re-maps a number from one range to another.

params.name: start1
params.description: lower bound of the source range.

params.name: stop1
params.description: upper bound of the source range.

params.name: start2
params.description: lower bound of the target range.

params.name: stop2
params.description: upper bound of the target range.

constrain.name: constrain
constrain.description: Constrains a value between a minimum and maximum.

lerp.name: lerp
lerp.description: Calculates a number between two numbers at a specific increment.

dist.name: dist
dist.description: Calculates the distance between two points.

sin.name: sin
sin.description: Returns the sine of an angle.

cos.name: cos
cos.description: Returns the cosine of an angle.

tan.name: tan
tan.description: Returns the tangent of an angle.

abs.name: abs
abs.description: Returns the absolute value of a number.

sqrt.name: sqrt
sqrt.description: Returns the square root of a number.

sq.name: sq
sq.description: Returns the square of a number (n * n).

pow.name: pow
pow.description: Returns the value of a number raised to an exponent.

textSize.name: textSize
textSize.description: Sets or gets the current text size.

textFont.name: textFont
textFont.description: Sets the font used by the text() function.

params.name: font
params.description: the font name or p5.Font object.

textAlign.name: textAlign
textAlign.description: Sets the way text is aligned when text() is called.

loadImage.name: loadImage
loadImage.description: Loads an image to create a p5.Image object.

image.name: image
image.description: Draws an image to the canvas.

loadSound.name: loadSound
loadSound.description: Loads a sound file from the given path.

millis.name: millis
millis.description: Returns the number of milliseconds since the sketch started.

second.name: second
second.description: Returns the current second as a value from 0 to 59.

minute.name: minute
minute.description: Returns the current minute as a value from 0 to 59.

hour.name: hour
hour.description: Returns the current hour as a value from 0 to 23.

day.name: day
day.description: Returns the current day as a value from 1 to 31.

month.name: month
month.description: Returns the current month as a value from 1 to 12.

year.name: year
year.description: Returns the current year as a four-digit value.

createVector.name: createVector
createVector.description: Creates a new p5.Vector with the given components.

params.name: angle
params.description: angle of rotation specified in radians.
